clinician.trajectory_summary: A 10-month-old infant presented with generalized hyperpigmentation and overgrowth; biochemical evaluation showed very low serum cortisol (<22 nmol/l) and very high ACTH (>1734 pg/ml) indicating isolated glucocorticoid deficiency. Physical examination confirmed overgrowth (> +3 SD height and weight) and hyperpigmentation involving mucosa and extremities. Developmental history showed marginal gross motor delay. Normal electrolytes and blood glucose excluded mineralocorticoid deficiency. An ACTH stimulation test demonstrated no cortisol response, confirming severe glucocorticoid deficiency. Treatment was initiated, and follow-up at 5 months showed clinical improvement with reduced pigmentation and slowed growth. No explicit clinical interpretation linking hyperpigmentation to elevated ACTH was documented, nor an explicit documented diagnosis of FGD, but the constellation of findings and treatment response strongly supports the diagnosis.
